title: Ayyub's spring
hook: strike the ground with your foot: a cool spring to wash and drink (38:41–44)

segments.voice: Yesterday: fitna, Dawud's test, and a ruling made after hearing one side. Your line was judge, then look at yourself.

A hot afternoon, years of illness behind you, your body aching, and someone hands you a glass of cold water. You drink it slowly. Then you splash some on your face, the back of your neck, your wrists. For a moment, that's everything. In Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayyub cried: harm has touched me, and You are the most merciful. Surah Sad tells what happened next, and the answer to years of suffering arrives in the most ordinary form there is. Water. Under his own feet.

Surah Sad, verse forty-one. Remember Our servant Ayyub, when he called his Lord: Satan has touched me with weariness and torment. Then verse forty-two, the answer, as a command: urkud bi-rijlik, strike the ground with your foot. And there it is: a spring, cool water to wash in and to drink. He has to do something. Not much: one stamp of a weak foot. But the healing comes through that small act, and through water, the plainest gift of all. Verse forty-three: and We gave him back his family, and as many again with them, a mercy from Us and a reminder for those with understanding. Then a stranger detail. Verse forty-four: take a bundle of grass in your hand and strike with it, and don't break your oath. Commentators explain that during his illness Ayyub had sworn to strike someone, many say his wife, a set number of times. Allah gave him a gentle way to keep his word without harming her: one tap with a bundle of stalks. Mercy for him, and mercy for her. Then the verdict: We found him patient. How excellent a servant! He was always turning back. A hadith in Bukhari adds one more picture. After his healing, while Ayyub was bathing, a shower of golden locusts fell, and he began gathering them. His Lord called: didn't I make you rich enough? And Ayyub answered: yes, but I can never do without Your blessing.
screen: `A COOL SPRING TO WASH AND DRINK.`
`A BUNDLE OF GRASS, AN OATH KEPT.`

segments.voice: If you can, go to a sink, let the water run cold, and wash your face slowly, once, twice, three times, feeling it on your forehead, your eyes, your cheeks. If you can't get up, picture it in detail. Then sit, damp-faced, with Ayyub's spring: the answer to years of waiting, in the plainest gift there is.
Ayyub's spring. After long illness, Ayyub is told to strike the ground with his foot, and a cool spring rises for washing and drinking. Today's word.
Your line: patient; a spring came. Patient in the long hardship, and grateful for every small gift after it. Day five hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims hold up Ayyub as the model of sabr, patience in illness and loss; his cry in 21:83 is often recited by the sick, and his story is told to comfort those in long hardship.

chat.says: How did Ayyub's long suffering finally end, in Surah Sad?
options: He was told to strike the ground with his foot, and a cool spring rose.
A healer from a nearby town finally found a cure for his illness.
He stopped praying about it, and the illness slowly faded away.
chat.meaning: Sad 38:42: strike the ground with your foot. A spring rose, cool water to wash in and drink, and his family was given back.
